title: Meta Instagram User access token in a token exchange response member
summary: A synthetic Instagram User access token as the access_token value of a data entry of the short-lived exchange response, and as the access_token member of the long-lived exchange response, bare and in a raw HTTP response.
rationale: Meta documents that the Instagram Login flow returns a short-lived Instagram User access token in a data entry and a long-lived one as the access_token member of a second response. The documentation states no prefix, alphabet or width, so the member name is the only identifying context and no bare-value rule is implied. The Instagram-scoped user id and the permissions string beside it are not the token. The Instagram token is kept separate from the Meta user access token: no shared carrier is assumed.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the value of the access_token member of an Instagram Login token exchange response is treated as a credential. Meta documents the exchange responses (carrier existence only); the value admission and extent are the project's decisions.

sources.supports: Capture the access_token value. This is the user’s short-lived Instagram User access token which your app can use to access Instagram API with Instagram Login endpoints.
sources.locator: Business Login for Instagram, Step 2. Exchange the Code For a Token

sources.supports: On success, your app receives a JSON response with your app user’s long-lived access token, the token type, and the expiration.
sources.locator: Business Login for Instagram, Step 3. Get a long-lived access token

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
